item.title: 6 Moments When Outside Perspective Changes Everything
item.description: When a situation is close, it's hard to get clear.

item.title: Where the rivers meet: Cahawba then and now
item.description: Long before Old Cahawba earned its reputation as a “ghost town,” it was a place filled with promise. When the U.S. began preparing for Alabama’s transition from territory to statehood, the meeting point of the Cahaba and Alabama Rivers stood out as a logical place for investment and growth.

item.title: Selma: The place we call ‘home’
item.description: One of the remarkable things about our wonderful town is her capacity to welcome folks from all over the world.

item.title: Why More Students Are Seeking Academic Writing Support Today
item.description: Life by students has changed rapidly. Courses move quickly. Expectations rise every year. In contemporary times, several students are maintaining classes, work and family responsibilities simultaneously. The middle of this pressure is student writing.

item.title: Former foster parent fights to buy back, reopen local youth facility
item.description: Dallas County resident Donald Shumate is on a mission to raise nearly half a million dollars to reclaim a dream more than 20 years in the making: a sanctuary for children in need.

item.title: VFW hosting event to help veterans get access to benefits
item.description: Selma’s Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) Post 3016 is hosting its Veterans Helping Veterans event on Thursday, Feb. 26, from 9 a.m. until 1 p.m. at the VFW, 299 Kingsbend Road in Selma.

item.title: Edmundite Missions offering nine-week Business Institute for Entrepreneurship
item.description: The Edmundite Missions Center for Workforce Development has recently announced the return of its annual program, the Edmundite Missions Business Institute for Entrepreneurship.

item.title: Celebrating the retirement of Robert Edwards, Jr.
item.description: After 37 years of exceptional service with Rountree Electric Supply Co., Robert Edwards, Jr. has officially retired.

item.title: Jo Ann Bland’s public viewing set for Friday
item.description: The Selma community is mourning the death of Jo Ann Bland, a civil rights icon and a co-founder of the National Voting Rights Museum and Institute who died on Thursday, Feb. 19, at the age of 72.
